Elroy Fernandes · 5 min read · 10.3K reads Figma Opens Its Canvas to AI Coding Agents, Answering Canva's Pivot Figma just told Claude Code and Cursor they can edit your design files directly. That's not a small feature update, it's a bet on who controls the next layer of creative work. At Config India in Bengaluru on October 15, 2026, Figma announced 20 new partners for its Model Context Protocol server, the open standard that lets outside AI agents read and write inside a Figma file. According to a report from Crypto Briefing, the new partner list includes Amp, ClickUp, Dia, Junie by JetBrains, Linear, Meta Muse, Mistral, Notion, OpenCode and Sarvam Agents. Figma had already opened a narrower version of this in March, bringing on five partners focused on turning code into editable canvas objects. This expansion is the company tripling down on the same bet. Here's what the protocol actually does. A tool like Claude Code or Cursor can now query a Figma file for its layout, type styles, color tokens and component structure, then write changes back into that file, not just read a flat export. Figma's own help documentation lists Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code and Codex among the supported clients. A developer no longer has to eyeball a PNG and guess the padding. The agent pulls the real auto-layout rules and component variants straight from the file. Not everyone at Figma is fully sold on the plumbing underneath it. Dylan Field, the company's co-founder, posted on X that MCP is "not a perfect protocol," pointing out that Anthropic, the company that created the standard, doesn't expose artifacts and other cloud resources created through MCP calls, which he said leaves asymmetric context-sharing problems unaddressed. It's a notable thing for a CEO to say in the same week his company adds 20 partners to that exact protocol. He's shipping the bet while publicly flagging its flaws. This is where the timing gets interesting. Back on April 16, 2026, at Canva Create in Los Angeles, chief operating officer Cliff Obrecht told the crowd that Canva was shifting from "a design platform with AI tools" to "an AI platform with design tools." The company launched Canva AI 2.0 around a new in-house foundation model it calls the Canva Design Model, built to understand design hierarchy well enough to orchestrate layout engines, asset libraries and typography on its own. Feed it a plain-English prompt, like "build me a 12-page pitch deck," and it hands back editable vectors, not a flattened image. TechCrunch reported that Canva's assistant can now call on multiple internal tools in sequence to assemble a design rather than generating one static output. sources.title: Figma Launches Specs to Help AI Agents Follow Design Rules
sources.snippet: TechCrunch published the news regarding Figma’s first Config event in India. This article describes the features, specifies what Figma stated about their philosophy, and explores what remains unsaid. ## What Figma Announced Figma announced a new Markdown-based editor that defines a company’s design, imports design and code libraries, and integrates with the Payload headless content management system. The announcements were made at the company’s first Config event in India. Through some of the features, Figma hopes to provide its own agents and third-party agents with a more comprehensive definition of a brand’s design rules, ensuring they are more likely to adhere to them when using AI to create designs or code. The other announcements relate to code, tooling, and content management. [...] ## Code Layers Move To Open Beta In addition, Figma has also opened up its code layers feature to users in open beta. Code layers bring coding to design on the canvas, making for more interactive prototypes. Figma announced the new feature in June in a private beta. This week, at an India event, the company opened up the feature to more users to test. TechCrunch uses the term open beta and public beta to refer to the stage. Users can also prompt the agent to turn a design into code, or tweak a section of it, to iterate on a prototype. ## More Code, Not More Releases [...] CALL US AT: Get in Touch With Us AI-Powered Design Workflow Studio Home » News » Figma Launches Specs To Help AI Agents

sources.title: Figma (FIG) Q3 earnings report 2026
sources.snippet:
Executives lifted the full-year forecast. Figma now anticipates an 11% operating margin, up from 9% as of August, and $1.497 billion to $1.499 billion in revenue, compared with $1.463 billion to $1.467 billion before. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were looking for $1.471 billion in 2026 revenue.

The company sees fourth-quarter revenue growth slowing to about 33%. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted 28% growth.

Figma's announcement comes a day after highly valued design software startup Canva said it would cut 22% of its employees. [...] The number of weekly users working at organizations that spend over $10,000 on Figma who used AI credits increased by almost 50% during the quarter, Figma said in the statement. The share of work the company's own AI model performs doubled, and the rate of people undoing AI-generated work has fallen.

"If there's certain actions that we can power for our customers at lower latency, lower cost, or similar quality to third party, we're open to that as well," Melwani said.

Executives will discuss the results with analysts on a conference call starting at 5 p.m. ET. [...] Shares have come down about 41% so far in 2026, while the S&P 500 index has gained 12%. Earlier this year, investors became concerned that artificial intelligence models could pose a competitive risk to Figma. Across much of software, AI panic has largely subsided as incumbents have posted persistent growth.

sources.snippet: ## People Also Ask Figma shares fell 12% despite beating Q3 2026 earnings estimates because the company announced it would bundle advanced AI features into existing subscriptions at no additional cost. This strategy sacrifices near-term revenue to lock in users and establish long-term market dominance in AI-powered design. Figma is bundling advanced AI features including auto-layout suggestions, intelligent component generation, and AI-powered design assistance into existing subscription tiers. The company reported that teams using these AI features are creating 30% more design files and collaborating at higher rates. [...] Figma just pulled off what should have been a victory lap, but Wall Street isn't celebrating. The collaborative design platform reported Q3 2026 results that topped analyst expectations across the board, yet shares tumbled as much as 12% in extended trading after the company revealed it's giving away what could have been a lucrative revenue stream. The culprit? Figma's decision to bundle advanced artificial intelligence features into existing subscription tiers without raising prices. It's the kind of move that makes strategic sense if you squint at the long game, but it sent investors scrambling to recalculate their models for 2027 and beyond.
